_about: Cap levels for post/run_cap.py. On the day, fill in the ofgem block from Ofgem's announcement (Great Britain average, Direct Debit, nil-kWh standing charges, VAT included at 0% on electricity and 5% on gas) and rerun. Every null in the ofgem block is a placeholder; the script emits no Ofgem figures until all of them are filled.

october.label: October to December 2026
october.source: Ofgem, energy price cap unit rates and standing charges, 1 October to 31 December 2026

cornwall.label: January to March 2027 (Cornwall Insight forecast)
cornwall.source: Cornwall Insight, final forecast of the January to March 2027 cap, press release of 18 November 2026

ofgem.label: January to March 2027 (Ofgem cap)
ofgem.source: Ofgem, energy price cap unit rates and standing charges, 1 January to 31 March 2027, and its letter of 25 November 2026 on the cap update

history._about: Table 1 and Figure 1: Ofgem's announced typical Direct Debit dual-fuel cap and the typical values it was quoted at; at_current_tdcv is the cap at 2,500 kWh and 9,500 kWh (PolicyEngine's calculation from Ofgem's average rates before July 2026; Ofgem's restatement for April to September 2026). Copied from the 19 November 2026 post.

peak_2022._about: For the 'why the cap changed' paragraph: the highest cap Ofgem set in 2022-23, as Ofgem states it on the day (its announcement often compares with it). Fill all four or leave all null; the post then shows a placeholder.
